solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Remove last of ancient vehicles from the east

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means reading right to left, so everything is turned around
the last of a word is its final letter, so only the end of ancient is kept

parts.note: the final letter of ancient
two vehicles, a cart and a bus

explanation.surface: Clearing away the final relic among some antique carriages that arrived from the east.
explanation.walkthrough: The vehicles are two separate ones, CART and BUS, which follow T before the whole string is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: To subtract is to take away or deduct, so it is a synonym of remove.

clue.text: Mate's back, wanting an E

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the named letter is missing from the word

parts.note: to espouse a cause is to back or support it
the letter itself, taken off the front

explanation.surface: Someone's partner has a bad back and is hoping for a top grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate's back' reads as a body part; the 's is just a link and back is the verb espouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate in the sense of a marriage partner is a husband or wife, which is what a spouse is.

clue.text: Reportedly second-choice goalie, one needing some protection

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the words are heard spoken rather than read

parts.note: the second-choice team is the B team, so its goalie is a B keeper

explanation.surface: Commentary on a reserve goalkeeper who needs shielding from the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: The protection is the veil and gloves worn when handling hives, not a defensive wall in front of a goal.
explanation.definitionFit: A person tending hives wears protective clothing against stings, so a beekeeper is someone needing some protection.

clue.text: What's specified in contract of theatre director on way up

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
of here means taken from within, so the letters come out of the words that follow

parts.note: sitting across the junction of the two words

explanation.surface: The demands written into a stage director's contract as their career climbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Famously, performers' riders list what they want provided backstage, so the definition fits the theatrical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an added clause or schedule of requirements attached to a contract, such as a performer's backstage demands.

clue.text: Party type, as Queen Camilla is?

parts.note: short for Conservative, a UK political party
a sort is a type or kind

explanation.surface: Asking what kind of party-goer Queen Camilla is.
explanation.walkthrough: Camilla's title for years was Queen Consort, the wife of the reigning King Charles III.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is the spouse of a reigning monarch, and Camilla's official title was Queen Consort.

clue.text: Trouble in top boys' school

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to distress or torment
second meaning: the famous English public school for boys in north-west London

explanation.surface: A boy at an elite school has got himself into bother.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrow is one of England's most famous fee-paying boarding schools, alma mater of Churchill.
explanation.definitionFit: To harrow is to cause distress, and Harrow is a leading English public school for boys.

clue.text: A foreign national, from Turkey perhaps

indicators.note: foreign suggests something made strange and unfamiliar, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An overseas citizen who may well be a Turk.
explanation.walkthrough: Anatolia is the Asian peninsula making up most of Turkey; 'perhaps' marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Anatolian describes someone or something from Anatolia, the region forming most of modern Turkey.

clue.text: Dance with sailor, keeling over after drink

parts.note: a spirit

indicators.note: a ship keeling over capsizes, turning upside down, which in a down clue flips the letters

parts.note: able seaman

explanation.surface: A drunken sailor dancing until he falls over.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Ready for a fight?

parts.note: surface reading: prepared and eager for combat
setter's reading: ready as in readies, slang for cash, so this is money set aside for a fight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' looks like an adjective meaning prepared, but it is a noun, as in 'the ready', meaning cash.
explanation.definitionFit: A war chest is a fund of money reserved for a campaign or conflict, literally the ready for a fight.

clue.text: More than one finished cooked to a frazzle?

wordplay.note: two words that each mean finished, as in the phrase over and done

explanation.surface: A cook finishes several dishes and leaves them burnt to a crisp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than one finished' asks for two synonyms of finished: OVER and DONE, which sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is overdone has been cooked too long, and a frazzle is the burnt extreme of that.

clue.text: The Speaker's destiny increasingly untroubled

indicators.note: a speaker's version is what is heard said out loud, not how it is written

parts.note: karma is fate or destiny

explanation.surface: The Commons Speaker's fate is to grow ever more serene.
explanation.walkthrough: The match relies on a non-rhotic British accent, where the r in calmer is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Calmer is the comparative of calm, meaning more untroubled than before.

clue.text: German chap baring bottom?

indicators.note: baring strips off the outer covering, so the outside letters go and the inner part stays

parts.note: the inside of the word with its first and last letters stripped

explanation.surface: A German man mooning someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German male first name, so it is an example of a German chap.

clue.text: Complete quiet always for the poet

parts.note: the hush sound asking for quiet
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever

explanation.surface: A poet demanding total, permanent silence.
explanation.walkthrough: Poets drop letters for metre, giving e'er for ever and o'er for over.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer means utter or absolute, as in sheer nonsense, so it is a synonym of complete.

clue.text: Poet's oath upset person with healing hands

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: every letter of the two words

explanation.surface: A poet's solemn vow distresses a faith healer.
explanation.definitionFit: An osteopath treats patients by manipulating bones and muscles by hand, a manual therapist.

clue.text: Bottle of gin perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: courage or nerve, as British slang has it
second meaning: a distilled alcoholic drink, of which gin is one

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bottle of gin; in fact bottle is British slang for courage, which is spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Spirit means courage or mettle, and also a strong distilled drink such as gin or vodka.

clue.text: Regret Sun somehow on the rise again

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive in some unstated other order

parts.note: every letter of the two words

explanation.surface: Sorry to see the sun rising once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Resurgent describes something reviving and gaining strength again after a decline.

clue.text: On reflection I think no American is threatening

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror is back to front, so the letters are read the other way

parts.note: the texting abbreviation for in my opinion
taken as written
abbreviation for United States

explanation.surface: Having thought it over, someone decides no American is menacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' sounds like 'having thought again' but it turns only IMO around.
explanation.definitionFit: Ominous means suggesting that something bad is about to happen, which is menacing or threatening.

clue.text: Spring in Nigeria almost too hot

indicators.note: almost means not quite the whole, so the word loses its final letter
hot can mean stirred up or agitated, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the word cut short by one letter

explanation.surface: Springtime in Nigeria is nearly too hot to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season, and 'too hot' like a weather report; spring is the verb, and hot is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring from something is to arise or come from it, which is to originate.

clue.text: Cast off wickedness? This woman won't

parts.note: to shed is to cast off, as a snake its skin
evil is wickedness

explanation.surface: An appeal to give up sin, which one woman refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the wordplay: she is the woman who won't shed evil, a she-devil.
explanation.definitionFit: A she-devil is a cruel, malicious woman, one who would never give up her wicked ways.

clue.text: Is Sarah making a hot sauce?

indicators.note: making means forming something new out of raw material, so these letters are reshaped

parts.note: every letter of the two words

explanation.surface: Wondering whether Sarah is preparing a spicy condiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Harissa is a fiery North African chilli paste, an example of a hot sauce.

clue.text: Mythical vessel slowly heading off

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, and off says that letter is removed

parts.note: the musical direction meaning slowly and broadly

explanation.surface: A legendary ship departing at a leisurely pace.
explanation.walkthrough: Largo is the Italian tempo marking for a very slow pace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts in Greek legend.

clue.text: Relative in Lubyanka finally set free

indicators.note: finally points at the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the final letter of Lubyanka
to untie is to loosen bonds and set free

explanation.surface: A family member at last released from the Lubyanka.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lubyanka is the Moscow headquarters and prison of the KGB.
explanation.definitionFit: An auntie is an informal word for an aunt, a family relative.

clue.text: Cruel for a Cockney, being without guile

indicators.note: Cockneys famously drop the h sound, so the word is as such a speaker would say it

parts.note: heartless means cruel, said without its opening h

explanation.surface: A Cockney who is cruel yet entirely innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner whose accent drops the h, so heart becomes 'art.
explanation.definitionFit: Artless means simple and natural, without cunning or deceit, which is being without guile.

clue.text: About to give up and go back

parts.note: re means concerning or about
to cede is to surrender or give up

explanation.surface: Someone about to quit and retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to move back or withdraw, as tide or a hairline does.

clue.text: Utterly depressed by the Tories?

parts.note: feeling down is feeling depressed
the Tories are the party of the political right

explanation.surface: Someone thoroughly miserable about the Conservative government.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday name for a member of Britain's Conservative Party, on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright is an adverb meaning thoroughly or completely, as in downright rude.

clue.text: Go round with something on your shoe?

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for with
the raised part at the back of a shoe

explanation.surface: Turning around with something stuck to your footwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something on your shoe' suggests mud or gum; it is the heel, part of the shoe itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To wheel is to turn or swing round in a circle, so it is a synonym of go round.

clue.text: Catch an Edith Piaf number

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to grab or take hold of
second meaning: the French word for sixteen, a number Piaf would use

explanation.walkthrough: A Piaf number looks like one of her songs; it is a number in her language, French.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize is to grab hold of, and seize is French for sixteen, a number the French singer Piaf would say.

clue.text: Hard-up family thrown into street

indicators.note: something thrown into a place ends up inside it

parts.note: standard abbreviation for street
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: A broke family evicted onto the street.
explanation.walkthrough: Skint is British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Skint is informal British for penniless, which is being hard-up.

clue.text: Panorama first to report on end of the Observer

parts.note: a panorama is a wide view

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so only that letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the word after it

parts.note: the opening letter of report

explanation.surface: A BBC current-affairs show is the first to report on the end of the Observer newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: Panorama is a BBC TV documentary programme and The Observer a Sunday newspaper; the R placed on the E means after it in an across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A viewer is someone who watches or looks on, which is an observer.

clue.text: Feel uneasy about information in hospital grounds

parts.note: H is the map symbol for hospital

indicators.note: in places one thing inside another

parts.note: an estate is a property's grounds
I is the symbol for an information point

explanation.surface: A patient anxious about the information posted around the hospital grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To hesitate is to pause through doubt or unease before acting.

clue.text: Precocious girl devouring old books in LA

indicators.note: something devouring another takes it inside itself

parts.note: Los Angeles
standard abbreviation for old
lit is short for literature

explanation.surface: A clever young girl in Los Angeles reading old books voraciously.
explanation.walkthrough: The title girl of Nabokov's novel has given her name to any sexually precocious young girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Lolita, from Nabokov's novel, has become a byword for a precocious, seductive young girl.

clue.text: A model wife at this point leaving husband? In a way

indicators.note: leaving means departing from, so the named letter goes out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
to sit for an artist is to model
standard abbreviation for wife
here means at this point
standard abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A model wife who walks out on her husband, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: As it were is a hedge meaning so to speak or in a manner of speaking, which is in a way.
